short: Raw-waveform front end and BGRU fusion (M06) are standard: they tie MFCC in clean LRW audio (97.7%), and the noise gains rest on one run with the same babble noise in training and test.
position: The paper [@petridis2018e2e] changes processing (M06): an 18-layer 1D ResNet on the raw waveform replaces spectral audio features, joined to a raw-pixel visual ResNet by concatenation and a two-layer BGRU, trained jointly. This is standard: raw waveform is the minority audio input among LRW audio-visual studies (18 against 29 with spectral features, pattern match, Appendix), and the best LRW audio-visual result, 98.76% [@ryumin2023sensors], uses log-Mel input. The raw front end ties a 2-layer MFCC BGRU in clean audio (97.7% each, Table 1), and its noise margin is measured against a baseline with no convolutional front end, so representation and depth change together. The audio-visual gain under noise holds in direction, but rests on one run, the same babble noise type and SNR range in training and test (§4.3, §5) and no fusion alternative; "significantly outperforms" (Abstract) has no test behind it. Evaluation (M12) is standard for AVSR.
